originalTitle: Tesla and SpaceX are discussing a possible merger, Musk says

content: Tesla and SpaceX have formed special committees to discuss a possible merger, Elon Musk said during the latter’s third quarter earnings call Tuesday. Musk, who serves as CEO of both companies, said the special committees were formed at the request of shareholders and consist of independent directors (though he did not name them). He also noted that he is not a member of either committee, nor involved in any of the discussions. “Because I’m a conflicted party, I can’t actually be in the discussions of the special committees,” Musk said. “So it’s an odd kabuki dance where two groups of people are talking and I can’t be in the conversation.” The groups have not reached agreement on the terms of any transaction — and there’s no guarantee that they will. “At the end of the day, the shareholders have to be supportive of this,” he continued. “And particularly on the Tesla side, we will need a 50 percent vote of all shares, not just those who vote, but of all shareholders. And that’s quite a high hurdle to try to achieve.” That said, Musk called the possibility of a Tesla-SpaceX merger a “good idea.” He continued: > I do think there’s a lot of merit to combining companies as we are pretty much in the superintelligence singularity. And there’s a lot to be gained from cooperating on developing superintelligence software, chip design, the TeraFab, obviously robotics, mass to orbit with the Starmind constellation, connectivity. So I think it would be a good idea, but it’s really up to the special committees of both companies. They’ve got to come up with something and then that’s going to be put to the shareholders as a vote. A Tesla-SpaceX merger would be a blockbuster corporate deal creating a mega-entity valued upwards of $3.6 trillion. But combining Musk’s car and energy company with his AI and rocket company would not be without its tradeoffs. A lot depends on which company absorbs the other. To buy SpaceX, Tesla would have to create millions of new stock shares, which for current Tesla owners would mean owning a smaller slice of a much larger pie. SpaceX’s launch goals require tens of billions of dollars every year — extra spending that could drain Tesla’s ability to build new car factories and battery plants. That said, most Wall Street analysts and legal experts believe SpaceX would acquire Tesla (or absorb it through a stock swap) rather than vice versa. Since its IPO, SpaceX has maintained a higher valuation than Tesla. A merger in that direction would allow SpaceX shareholders to hold the majority control of the combined mega-entity. Some Tesla shareholders may balk at this deal. But it would also create one company for those who believe in Musk’s vision of the future — robot cars, humanoid robots, AI super-intelligence, and human habitats on Mars — in which to place their investments. And Tesla shareholder approved Musk’s enormous pay package last year — even after a Delaware judge tossed it over lack of independence. Earlier this month, Barclays published a client note suggesting a potential Tesla-SpaceX combination could be announced ahead of Tesla’s annual shareholder meeting scheduled for December 3, 2026.

chineseContent: 埃隆·马斯克在周二的第三季度财报电话会议上表示，特斯拉和 SpaceX 已经成立了特别委员会来讨论可能的合并。担任两家公司首席执行官的马斯克表示，特别委员会是应股东的要求成立的，由独立董事组成（尽管他没有透露姓名）。他还指出，他不是这两个委员会的成员，也没有参与任何讨论。 “因为我是一个冲突方，所以我实际上无法参与特别委员会的讨论，”马斯克说。 “所以这是一种奇怪的歌舞伎舞蹈，两组人在说话，而我不能参与谈话。”这些集团尚未就任何交易条款达成一致，而且也不能保证他们会达成一致。 “最终，股东必须支持这一点，”他继续说道。 “特别是在特斯拉方面，我们需要所有股份的 50% 投票权，不仅仅是投票者，而是所有股东。这是一个相当高的障碍。”尽管如此，马斯克仍称特斯拉与 SpaceX 合并的可能性是一个“好主意”。他继续说道： > 我确实认为合并公司有很多优点，因为我们几乎处于超级智能奇点。通过合作开发超级智能软件、芯片设计、TeraFab、显然是机器人技术、Starmind 星座的质量到轨道、连接性，我们可以获得很多收获。所以我认为这是一个好主意，但这实际上取决于两家公司的特别委员会。他们必须想出一些办法，然后提交给股东投票。 Tesla 和 SpaceX 的合并将是一项轰动一时的企业交易，将创建一个价值超过 3.6 万亿美元的巨型实体。但将马斯克的汽车和能源公司结合起来
